The Best Sport Touring Gear UK 2026: Built for the Long Haul

The best sport touring gear in the UK is defined by one demanding requirement: it has to keep you comfortable, dry and protected for a full day in the saddle, then do it again tomorrow. A sport tourer is the machine that genuinely does everything, carrying you and a pillion and a week of luggage up the length of the country with the pace to enjoy the good roads when they arrive. The gear has to be just as capable, prioritising all-day comfort, proper waterproofing and a cut that works with luggage and a fairing rather than against them.

These are the bikes I choose when the plan is big miles, from a full run of the NC500 to a fast blast over the Bealach na Ba and back down through the Highlands on the A82. The kit below is chosen for riders who measure their days in hundreds of miles rather than minutes of thrills. For the bike-side companion, read our guide on how to tour on a sport tourer.

The Jacket Is the Heart of the System

On a sport tourer your jacket works harder than any other piece of kit, because you are wearing it through every weather Britain can conjure in a single day. A laminated Gore-Tex construction is the gold standard, keeping the membrane on the outside so the shell does not soak up water and chill you. Big, well-placed vents matter just as much, because a jacket that cannot dump heat becomes a portable sauna on a warm run.

The Rev'It Dominator 3 GTX Jacket is a benchmark all-rounder that stays dry through hours of rain yet vents well when the sun appears. If that stretches the budget, the Richa Atlantic 2 GTX Textile Jacket delivers most of the same all-weather ability for far less. Our guide to textile touring jackets compares the leading options in detail.

All-Day Comfort Is the Real Goal

Sport touring is an endurance discipline, and comfort is what lets you keep enjoying it hour after hour. The details that seem minor on a short ride become critical over three hundred miles.

  • Fit for the riding position. A sport tourer leans you slightly forward, so a jacket cut a touch longer in the arms and back stops it riding up and exposing your wrists and lower back.
  • Adjustability. Waist, arm and collar adjusters let you fine-tune the fit as you add or remove layers through the day.
  • Ventilation you can reach. Vents you can open with gloves on, at speed, are worth their weight in gold when the weather changes mile to mile.
  • Neck comfort. A soft, adjustable collar stops the chafing that ruins a long day behind a tall screen.

Waterproof Boots You Can Walk In

Sport touring boots need to protect at speed, stay bone dry in a downpour, and still be comfortable enough to walk around a service station or a hotel car park. A tall waterproof touring boot with a Gore-Tex membrane and enough ankle armour is the sweet spot, avoiding both the flimsiness of a fashion boot and the clumping bulk of a race boot.

The Sidi Aria Gore-Tex Boots are a superb all-day touring boot, waterproof and supportive yet genuinely comfortable to walk in when you finally stop for the night after a long haul up the A9.

Gloves That Handle a Changing Day

The great challenge of sport touring gloves is that a single day can swing from warm sunshine to cold rain and back. A clever answer is a glove with both a vented and a waterproof chamber, so you adapt to the weather without carrying three pairs.

The Held Air N Dry II Gloves do exactly that, giving you airflow when it is dry and a waterproof chamber to slide into when the rain starts, all in one glove. It is a design that could have been invented specifically for British sport touring.

The best sport touring kit is the kit that adapts without stopping. Every time you have to pull over to change gloves, add a layer or dig out a rain suit, you lose momentum and comfort. Choose gear that flexes on the move.

Luggage-Friendly Kit and Real Panniers

A sport tourer is built to carry proper luggage, and your gear should work with it rather than fight it. Avoid jackets with large rear pockets or flapping panels that foul a top box, and choose a cut that sits comfortably against a pannier-loaded bike. Hard panniers are the natural choice for a sport tourer, secure, weatherproof and lockable for when you leave the bike at a hotel.

A set like the Givi Trekker Outback Panniers gives you generous, weatherproof, lockable storage that transforms a sport tourer into a genuine two-up touring machine. For the full picture on fitting and choosing luggage, our motorcycle panniers guide covers every system.

Heated Grips and Season-Stretching Extras

Because sport touring is about riding whatever the calendar says, cold-weather comfort features earn their place. A set of Oxford Heaterz Premium Heated Grips keeps your hands working on a frosty start over Snake Pass or Hartside on the A686, and they let you run thinner, more comfortable gloves in the shoulder seasons. Add a neck tube and a thermal base layer and you have a system that copes with a British spring, which is to say all four seasons before lunch.

Matching Gear to Your Sport Tourer

The exact kit that suits you depends on how you use the bike. A rider covering huge two-up miles on a Kawasaki Versys 1000 SE wants the very best weather protection and the most comfortable, adjustable jacket. Someone on a sharper, sportier tourer like the Yamaha Tracer 9 GT might favour a slightly closer-fitting jacket to cut through the wind on faster roads. And a rider making relaxed, refined miles on a Honda NT1100 can lean hardest into comfort and luggage integration. Whatever you ride, prioritise all-day comfort, uncompromising waterproofing and luggage-friendly design, and a sport tourer will carry you across Britain in the effortless style it was built for.
